sections.h2: Selling a house in Chanhassen: your options
sections.html:
Three paths lead to a closing in Chanhassen: hire an agent, line up your own buyer, or take a cash offer. Prices here run high, which means a staged listing and an as-is sale can land far apart. Ask for both numbers before choosing, and ask what each route would cost you in repairs, fees and carrying costs while the house sits.

  • Agent: best for an updated house when you can host open houses.
  • Private sale: works if the buyer is already known to you, like a neighbor or relative.
  • Cash buyer: fits an estate house, a failing septic system, or a move that cannot wait on a school year or new job.

Owners occupy 84.1% of Chanhassen's homes, so the people a buyer meets on the block are mostly long-term residents rather than tenants.

Chanhassen is mostly in Carver County, about 15 miles southwest of Minneapolis, with a small eastern piece in Hennepin County. Main roads are U.S. Highway 212 and Minnesota Highways 5 and 41. Chanhassen incorporated as a city in 1967, and the population estimate for July 2025 is 25,748. Lakes such as Lake Ann, Lake Minnewashta and Lotus Lake, plus 70 miles of trails, give listing photos plenty to work with.

The 2020 rental vacancy rate was 8.5%, a number to weigh when pricing a house that tenants occupy.

Buyers skew toward established families. The 2020 count found a median age of 40.9, married couples heading 64.9% of households, and children in 36.8% of them. About 90.1% of residents stayed put for a full year, so listings often come from owners with long tenure and substantial equity. Another 15.4% of residents are 65 or older, which feeds a steady supply of downsizers.

If you are selling an inherited house, buyers will hold it up against updated listings at much higher prices. An as-is offer reflects the work the buyer takes on, not the neighborhood's median.

sections.h2: Which school district serves your Chanhassen address?
sections.html:
Most of Chanhassen lies in Eastern Carver County Schools, District 112. Students usually attend Bluff Creek or Chanhassen Elementary, Pioneer Ridge Middle School and Chanhassen High School.

The northern sections belong to the Minnetonka School District, District 276, with students usually going to Clear Springs or Excelsior Elementary, Minnetonka Middle School West and Minnetonka High School. Private options downtown include Chapel Hill Academy and St. Hubert Catholic School. The district line can run through a neighborhood, so ask the district to confirm the address before it goes into a listing.

A parcel that lacks city sewer or water brings extra paperwork. Rural lots most often have private systems, and Minnesota sets two separate disclosures for them.

  • Sewage: before the purchase agreement, you must state in writing whether household sewage goes to a permitted facility or to a subsurface treatment system, and attach any earlier inspection report (Minnesota Statutes section 115.55, subdivision 6). Staying quiet about a known system can leave the seller paying for compliance work if the buyer sues within two years of closing.
  • Wells: you must disclose known wells in writing, and the deed needs a well statement or a certificate with a $54 fee (section 103I.235). Liability for an undisclosed well can run six years from closing.

Carver County treats the subsurface sewage treatment disclosure as required on all property transfers. If you are unsure what is buried in the yard, ask the city's building staff and your title company early.

Chanhassen requires a license for any property rented for fewer than 30 consecutive days, even if it happens only a couple of times a year. The rule took effect January 1, 2023, and ordinary month-to-month leases fall outside it.

The license costs $200 a year, is renewed by February 1, and requires a Minnesota state lodging license. Its terms set the maximum number of overnight guests and vehicles and require compliance with the nuisance ordinance, including a 10 p.m. to 7 a.m. limit on amplified sound. Three notices of violation within 365 days mean revocation, and the owner cannot hold a short-term rental license again for seven years. Neighbors can report problems to a 24/7 hotline at 952-260-4995. If you are listing the house, take down any active short-term listing before the first showing.

Most Chanhassen deeds go to Carver County Land Records and Vitals, 600 East 4th Street, Chaska (952-361-1930). The counter runs weekdays 8 to 4:30. Parcels in the Hennepin County sliver are recorded by Hennepin County instead, and your tax statement shows which county applies.

A Carver deed package carries the recording fee, state deed tax, a $5 agricultural conservation fee, a certificate of real estate value for consideration above $3,000, well information, the sewage treatment disclosure, a full legal description, a complete notary acknowledgment, a drafted-by statement and a send-tax-statements-to line. Staff cannot choose a form or give legal advice, so lean on your title company or attorney. The deed tax under section 287.21 is 0.33% of net consideration.

sections.h2: What a buyer will ask you for
sections.html:
Any buyer, cash or financed, will ask for the same short list: the written sewage and well statements, the permit history for big projects, the tax statement showing which county and school district apply, and proof of who holds title. Collect those first. If the house has a septic system, find the last inspection report in your files before you talk to anyone.

A cash buyer subtracts repair costs from the price, so a clear description of known problems helps the offer arrive faster and stay put. When you compare offers, look at the closing date and the conditions as well as the dollar figure.

Timing varies with the file. A clean title and no mortgage can close in a couple of weeks. A payoff, a lien or a recording question on the Hennepin side can add days, so ask the title company which of those apply to you. Once the deed is signed, the title company handles the filing and the county sends the recorded document back.

faqs.q: Will a cash buyer take a Chanhassen house with a septic problem?
faqs.a: Many will, because they buy as is and subtract the repair from the offer. The written sewage disclosure is still yours to provide, along with any inspection report in your files.

faqs.q: Which county records a Chanhassen deed?
faqs.a: Carver County, for almost the whole city. The small eastern portion is in Hennepin County, and your tax statement names the county for your parcel.

faqs.q: Can I run Airbnb stays at my Chanhassen home while it is listed?
faqs.a: Only with the $200 annual city license plus a Minnesota lodging license, since any stay under 30 consecutive days counts. Skip it during showings and avoid the enforcement risk.

faqs.q: What is the deed tax on a Chanhassen sale?
faqs.a: It is 0.33% of net consideration, collected when the deed is recorded. Your title company will show the exact amount on the closing statement.

faqs.q: Which school district covers a Chanhassen address?
faqs.a: District 112, Eastern Carver County Schools, covers most of the city, and Minnetonka's District 276 covers the north. Look up the exact address before advertising a school.
